title: Two brothers, two choices
hookLine: the giant tells his brother he's wrong, and goes to fight for him anyway
carry: dharma first, even before a brother

cards: Kumbhakarna walks into Ravana's hall, still huge with sleep, and Ravana pours it all out. Rama has crossed the sea. Our best warriors are dead.
I lost today. You're the only one left who can save us. The court waits for the giant's roar.
And Kumbhakarna, the brother known for sleeping and eating, says what only Vibhishana has said to the king's face, and Vibhishana was driven out for it.

teach.h: WE TOLD YOU THIS WOULD HAPPEN.
teach.b: We told you, he says. At your council, this is exactly what we said would happen. A king who acts first and thinks afterward, who ignores good advice, brings disaster on himself.
You took another man's wife. This is the result. Ravana's face darkens.
He wants a champion, not a lecture. And Kumbhakarna sees his brother hurting, and softens. Enough, he says.
Whatever you did, I'm your brother. I'll go and kill your enemy. On the battlefield he's terrifying.
The monkeys scatter, and Angada has to shame them into turning back. He seizes Sugriva and carries him off under his arm, until Sugriva tears at the giant's ears and nose and escapes.
In the end Rama brings him down with his arrows. The Tamil poet Kamban adds a scene. Before the fight, Vibhishana comes to his brother on the field and begs him to join Rama.
Kumbhakarna refuses gently: you did right, you stay with Rama; my place is with our brother.
So the Ramayana sets two brothers side by side, and both told Ravana the truth to his face. One left to stand with dharma, what is right, and Rama welcomed him.
The other let love for his brother carry him into a wrong war, and fell. Many readers admire Kumbhakarna's honesty and his loyalty. But the epic honors Vibhishana's choice.
Telling the truth isn't enough if you then march with the wrong.

teach.h: DHARMA FIRST, EVEN BEFORE A BROTHER.
teach.b: Dharma first, even before a brother.

how: Kumbhakarna's rebuke of Ravana and his loyalty are much discussed in Ramayana storytelling, and Kamban's Tamil scene of the two brothers, Vibhishana and Kumbhakarna, meeting on the battlefield is often recited.

o: Ravana's giant brother, who warns him, then fights for him
a giant who sleeps through the war and never fights
Ravana's general, who urges him to keep fighting

games.q: the giant's choice — tap the pairs.
p: we told you this would happen
wanted a champion, not a lecture
carried off under the giant's arm
adds the brothers' meeting on the field

s: Kumbhakarna tells Ravana he was right to take Sita
he tells him plainly it was wrong, and that disaster was predicted.
he fights for Ravana anyway, out of loyalty
he says that whatever Ravana did, he's still his brother.
the Ramayana honors Vibhishana for leaving his brother's side
he told Ravana the truth and stood with dharma, and Rama welcomed him.

games.q: your best friend is about to do something you know is wrong, and asks for your help. by the Ramayana's two brothers, what's dharma?
o: tell them the truth kindly, and don't join in.
say nothing and stay out of it.
games.why: Kumbhakarna told the truth, then marched with the wrong anyway. Vibhishana told it and stood with dharma. the epic honors the second.

practice: Think of someone you love who is doing something you know isn't right. If you pray, hold them before God by name, and ask for what Vibhishana had: the courage to be honest and kind at once.
If you don't, breathe in their name, and breathe out the true thing you'd say to them, gently.

wordCard.voice: Kumbhakarna. The giant who tells Ravana plainly he's wrong, and then dies fighting for him out of a brother's loyalty, beside Vibhishana, who chose dharma.

orig.note: Sanskrit bhrātā: brother; the word at the heart of Kumbhakarna's answer to Ravana.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma first, even before a brother. Lakshmana's best day, and his worst, is next. See you then.
